messages.subject: Re: plotcorr Positive Correlation Plot color issue (Rattle 2.6.21, R 2.15.2, Mac Mountain Lion OS 10.8.2)
messages.subject_clean: plotcorr Positive Correlation Plot color issue (Rattle 2.6.21, R 2.15.2, Mac Mountain Lion OS 10.8.2)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ray,

Thanks for the feedback.

I've run some other datasets through Rattle to display some ordered Pearson correlation plots. So far they've all come out as expected. For example the one in Fig 5.16 of the Rattle book is what I still get with the latest versions.

Is there any possibility the data is different to what you had previously? If you had some way to demonstrate the difference it would help debug. I'm not aware of any changes to Rattle's calling of the ellipse functions.

Thanks,
Graham

Regards,
Graham

On 29 October 2012 09:45, Ray <raydigi...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello Everyone,
>
> I ran a plotcorr in rattle and am seeing some possible bugs.
>
> I imported the famous heart disease dataset from UCI's Machine Learning Repository.  I have attached the dataset to this email.
>
> Then I ran an ordered pearson correlation plot in the "Explore" tab of rattle.  However, the plot is showing different behavior than expected.
>
> When I ran this same plot on the same dataset in earlier versions of rattle, I noticed that there were some blue dots (positive correlations) on the plot (which are now shown as white dots).
>
> Note that rattle is calling the "plotcorr" function which is in R's "ellipse" package.  I am not sure if the ellipse package code has changed or the way that rattle "calls" the ellipse package has changed...
>
> My specs are:
> Rattle 2.6.21, R 2.15.2, Mac Mountain Lion OS 10.8.2
>
> Best Regards,
>
> Ray DiGiacomo, Jr.
> Healthcare Predictive Analytics Specialist

messages.body_plain:
Hi Graham,

I think the dataset has stayed consistent.  I think the issue may be the train/test/eval splits.

If I use 70/30/0 I get a correlation plot with no blue areas and if I use 80/20/0 I get a plot with blue areas.

However, I remember using the default train/test/eval rattle settings on the older version of rattle with an older version of R.  I believe the old default rattle settings were 70/30/0 or 70/15/15 - but I could be remembering incorrectly.

I will let you know if I encounter any other issues like this.  This may be tough to debug as of now.

Thanks for your help thus far.

- Ray

messages.subject: Re: graphs for ROC, Lift don't work
messages.subject_clean: graphs for ROC, Lift don't work
messages.body_plain:
The prediction function comes from ROCR. Rattle should be checking that you have ROCR installed but seems not to be doing so. You could try

> install.packages("ROCR")
> library(ROCR)

Hopefully that would help!

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Displaying output
messages.body_plain:
When I run a logistic regression, say, I get the first three columns COEFF ESTIMATE STD.ERROR
and then I get three more columns COEFF ZVALUE P(>|Z|).  I have to scroll up and down to look at the estimate and then the p-value.

I would like to get all five columns at once:  COEFF ESTIMATE STD.ERROR ZVALUE  P(>|Z|) so that I can see the estimate and the p-value at once.

I need to change the display width of the output, but I don't know how to do it in rattle.
